subject: Reuse the complete current compiler pair and measure foreign-binding construction costs
claim: All 27 foreign-binding cases pass. Fully cold compiler/application construction took 3568735 ms, with 1735 ms summed across the behavior cases. With equally warm lower-level caches the prior coordinator took 7324 ms and current compiler-pair reuse took 4492 ms. First pair publication using preserved products took 10089 ms. Both target WVB identities are unchanged. The existing split-cache owner passes its expanded 23-case sentinel on Windows and Debian; no new verifier entry point was added.

source.value: Worktree based on 5efd90a57e00b4d7fa96208f810402c68bb092fb. Exact implementation hashes are in the current pair run artifacts. The cold baseline used that unchanged commit.

runs.host: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations 10.0.26200, AMD Ryzen 9 3900X, Node 24.18.0
runs.target: Fresh compiler/application construction, two fixture products and all 27 cases; sampled tree working set reached 948871168 bytes

Four existing split-development groups including the expanded 23-case cache sentinel

limitations: Cold versus warm timings are different cache states; this change alone did not reduce genuinely cold construction to seconds. The fair warm comparison is 7324 ms versus 4492 ms.

The prior coordinator and its unchanged foreign-binding owner were copied from 5efd90a5 into private artifacts. Only script-directory and coordinator-path bindings were adapted; producers, arguments, fixtures, packaging and behavior cases were retained. Both comparison commands include the same approximately half-second key-inspection harness overhead.

The full Linux foreign-binding workload, cold Linux compiler-pair construction, complete database qualification and paired-host repository qualification were not run. The ordinary cold and complete qualification targets remain open.
The approved baseline was capped at 60 minutes and completed once. Read-only inspection and brief draft cache cases ran concurrently; this was not an isolated host benchmark.

Memory is a sampled process-tree maximum, not the true peak. Initial samples were manual; later samples were 15 seconds apart. CPU samples omit processes that ended before observation. The short warm runs were not memory-profiled.
Performance observations are single before/after samples, not stable regression thresholds. Cache protection is development construction evidence; every requested behavior still executes.
